The symbolic construct sHR encapsulates cumulative habit strength, while temporal relation HS(Δt) reflects the sensitivity of habit formation to stimulus-response timing. Reinforcement nature and amount introduce heterogeneity into the habit kernel, enabling adaptive behavior. These primitives form a dual structure: one rooted in biological necessity (innate behavior, need conditions), the other in learned association (conditioned stimuli, secondary reinforcement). Failure modes include temporal misalignment leading to habit decay, and reinforcement mismatch causing suboptimal policy convergence. The system exhibits nonlinearity through saturation effects and exponential decay in temporal relations, suggesting a potential for bifurcation under extreme conditions.
